definitions.regular: a season with >= 300 MLB PA (hitter) or >= 150 MLB BF (pitcher); MLB = level_id 1 of the dump's per-game files, summed per player and season
definitions.outcome: the player ever had a regular season, either way, through the last dump
definitions.cohort: players first seen at age <= 20 in dumps 2025-2484 who were ever in an org (level R, A, AA, AAA or MLB); hitters / pitchers by the role they held in most dumps
definitions.observation: one player-dump at ages 16-26, in an org at that dump, with the previous game-year's dump present; the same player counts once per age
definitions.age: the dump's Age field: the Jan-1 age, dump_<year> being dated Jan 1 of year+1
definitions.pot: the OOTP Pot grade of that dump (1-point steps, 20-80)
definitions.role: P when the dump position is SP, RP or CL, else H
definitions.core_skills: H: BABIP GAP POW EYE K (raw BABIP Gap Pow Eye Ks); P: STU HRR PBABIP CON (raw Stf HRA PBABIP Ctrl); a skill's display value is the mean of its vR and vL ratings
definitions.growth: sum over the core skills of (display now - display at the previous dump) / 5, over one game-year, rounded to 0.5; half steps occur because a display value is a vR/vL mean
definitions.pot_dir: up / flat / down by the Pot grade change over the previous dump, Pot >= 45 only
definitions.core_sum: sum over the core skills of underlying(display value)
definitions.internal_scale: band middles 20:115.5 25:153.5 30:198 35:249.5 40:299 45:348.5 50:393.5 55:424.5 60:443 65:457 70:471.5 75:485.5 80:505 85:559; 85 and above = 559; below 20 = 115.5; a display value between two bands interpolates linearly (a vR/vL mean can end in 2.5)
definitions.typical: mean and population sd of core_sum per age and Pot bucket, all outcomes pooled, same observations as grid
definitions.pot_only: odds by age and Pot bucket alone, over every in-org observation at 16-26 with or without a previous dump; for a player whose growth is unknown
definitions.cells: every cell ships with its n; cells with n < 15 are thin and the consumer decides

peak_definition: eventual peak WAA of the DEV players in a cell: per observation, the max of the player's engine now_WAA over his dumps at ages >= the cell age (BLM engine calibration, neutral park, from vintages/DEV/.waa_cache); only players seen at age >= 27 count, so the peak is realized; ceiling = the engine's ceiling_WAA at the observation's dump, the same number the app lists as MAX WAA P / WAP; p10-p90 and mean describe the eventual peak; listed_gap = mean of (eventual peak - ceiling); reach_share = share whose eventual peak >= that dump's ceiling; gain_p25 / gain_p50 / gain_p75 / gain_mean describe (eventual peak - the player's now_WAA at the observation's dump), never below 0 because the peak includes that dump; gain_n = rows with a priced now_WAA (at most n); the app's growth target is current WAA + gain_p50; mlb_share = share of the cell whose eventual peak reached -1 WAA (an MLB-level player, a 5th starter or bench bat; user, 2026-09-24: 'if they will ever be anything in the mlb'), useful_share = share that reached 0 WAA (an average MLB player), good_share = share that reached +1.5 (a clear regular), bars in peak_bars (user, 2026-09-24: Make it % is playing time, these say whether the lookalikes turned out good enough); those three shares are the cell's peak distribution and ignore the player's own current WAA, so a player already at the bar could read under 100% (user, 2026-09-24: 'there are a ton of guys who are already at 0+ WAA that are getting like tagged as less than 100% to reach it'); the conditional rule fixes that: gain_grid = the cell's gains at quantiles 5, 10, ..., 95 (19 values, 2 decimals) over every priced row, grid[i] being the gain at level (i + 1) * 5 percent; by_now = the same grid per now-WAA tercile (3 sub-cells cut at the cell's own now terciles, each with lo / hi = its now range, n, mlb / useful / good = the share of the sub-cell's eventual peaks at or above each bar, and gain_grid), only when the cell has >= 15 priced rows, else null; dev_signals picks the sub-cell holding the player's current WAA (nearest when outside, whole cell when the sub-cell has n < 15) and reads each bar's chance as the share of that grid at or above (bar - his current WAA): 1.0 when he is already at the bar, else linear between the grid levels; a player whose current sits outside every sub-cell's range (above the top hi or below the bottom lo) reads the nearest sub-cell's own mlb / useful / good instead, because the gain rule would lend him gains measured on players who were never where he is; peak uses the grid's observations, peak_pot_only the pot_only ones; cells with n < 15 are thin
